svg.aria-label: Fig. M1 Fetch, cycle by cycle, and the three redirect tiers
svg.text: Fig. M1 Fetch, cycle by cycle, and the three redirect tiers
One fetch group per cycle. The next fetch predictor answers in one cycle; the slower predictors check it two cycles later; decode and execute check again.
full history lookup, compare with the NFP answer
L0 miss: target from the L1I line
resolve, 13 cycles back to fetch in all
L0 hit: next PC ready for cycle 1, zero bubble
cycle 3 restart: L1 tier (two bubbles) or a slow predictor that disagrees (staged redirect)
hit gives target, length, end type
Next fetch predictor entry, as inferred from the fetch group behaviour
fields (widths are mine, the field set is from the claims)
len: up to 16 instructions, one 64 B line, cut at the first taken branch
end type: cond, uncond, call, return (RAS gives the target), indirect (ITTAGE gives it)
way: the L1I way to read so the tag array and iTLB can be skipped (patent)
pred mask: which slow predictors this group needs, the rest clock gated (patent)
training: written by the slow predictors when they disagree; kept until wrong twice; a new entry that
meets a strong set goes to a FIFO overflow table (patent)
Phantom fetch: a non branch at a trained PC redirects fetch, so the tag does not cover the full PC and
a hit is not verified against the instruction bytes until decode. Measured.
PC bits used by the zero bubble tier
512 sets x 2 ways = 1024 entries: PC[10:2] picks a set per instruction slot in a 2 KiB window, the two ways cover a 4 KiB footprint (measured)
Within 4 KiB a taken branch costs nothing; past it the second tier adds two bubbles, read as the L1 BTB
being coupled to the L1I: about 8192 entries, one per 8 B of the 192 KiB I-cache would be 24576, so
the 8192 looks like one target slot per 24 B, or a tagged side table. Open.
My reading: the L0 BTB is the fetch group table itself, one structure, with the 2 way sets
indexed by PC[10:2] so branches 2 KiB apart share a set; a probe with three taken branches
exactly 2 KiB apart would show the third evicting one of the first two.
1 taken branch per cycle in all cases; no trace cache on the M1 (ocxtal measured, Handley places it on M4).
depth unknown, Handley guesses at least 120
loop buffer source, no timing change
skipped short forward branch bodies deleted
NOP and B take no issue slot but keep a retire slot
shifted ALU op: one uop, issues twice
LDP: one uop, two register writes
pre and post index: extra base update uop
fusion pairs marked here, merged at map
main stack of 50 at decode, exact push and pop
small fetch side stack for returns whose calls decode has not seen
overflow clears the stack, call/return cost jumps
PAC bits checked where the stack is pushed and popped
